chapter: A difficult club job and closing
title: The demanding woman who runs a club job
summary: Joseph complains of a club owner who demands hard numbers, interferes with the band and cannot keep musicians.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: You know what they tell me? I was in that other night. Better have a white fella come there and give the boy, I believe, fifty dollars to play some numbers. You know what she tell the boy? Play what I want. Yeah, I know.
That's what they all jacked up. Yeah.

She's terrible. Well, I think that she's killed them boys. I'll tell you something, I'll play the man numbers. Man, they paid them. And they played it. Man, she come there and raise some time. Next time you do that, you don't have no job. See what I've been, Thomas? I see you get you somebody. None of them white boys want to work there.
She's terrible.
She called me up many times. Did she call me up?
No ma'am, not me.

No. And see the union, you can't force you to go there. That woman wake you too hard. Man, you know she pick up on all them old town numbers like old, what you call it? High-side, high-side, high-side, sweet Georgia Brown. And all them old red book numbers. Like Coca-Cola Hagen and all that. And all that's hard on your lip. That'd be different than they had another trumpet player there. That's right. That's what they really need in that place, two trumpets. That's what they need in that place, two trumpets. Well yeah, but she's not going to let you do that. No ma'am, she's not going to let you do that. No ma'am, she's not going to get along. Like I told Miss Plenty, I said Miss Plenty, I said Miss Plenty, I don't want to let you go to the side of the stuff like된 된 stuff like된 된 stuff like된
! And stuff like된

She's not going to let you do that. No, man, she's hard to get along. Like I told Ms. Plenty, I said, Ms. Plenty, I'd be glad to work with Octavia. Octavia's a nice fellow. Well, that is not Octavia, it's that woman's so much help. She's helped, man, and she keep that job. She keep that job. No good nothing at all, nothing like that, man. A woman will kill you. She take your honor. Why you think she could get a white band? Don't you know she'd have a white band there? She can't get any. She like, like Louis Premham, I come up with him. Louis Premham want no job like that.
No.

Louis Premham couldn't stand him one night. Not what she put on you. Man, you got to have, you got to have this to work with Steve Plenty. Man, need a dollar, mine is better to work for her. And she's going to try to get along, Bill. She's come to try with her cousin sometimes. I heard, yeah. I heard that. She's come to try with her cousin. She interfere with you. Tell you to tell the band something. She tell them to do what she wants to. Now you don't be doing that. Be doing that shit.
Yeah, it's amazing that she hasn't run out of musicians by now. She's been through most of the other players. She can't get nobody.

She can't get, well I tell you, I tell you, she's the only one that's going to be able to play around there for her. Nobody can't stand it. Man, you couldn't get no youngsters from putting that. Now that's what you call, that's where old man is sure where you need it.
Yeah.
That's a hard job, man. Do you know them boys at the, at the corner don't play hard? Is that the famous though?
Them white boys don't play hard.

Them white boys get resets and get on and go have their fun. Sure. They get three, they get, they get four resets a day. And my mother's relented, you only get two. I believe they knock off around one o'clock, they get resets. And come back again. Lucky play piano, got a boy called, you know Lucky. Yeah. He play piano in the team. And Lucky's winning worse than enough. Yeah.
Sure.

Lucky tells everything, go on. They tell me. Yeah. That's their shit, there's no use in being around that kind of people Bill. A man want, a man want money. What I mean you want money, but you want money in the right kind of way. You want nobody to try to kill you. Right. You understand? What she try to do, she try to drive you like she drive cars. But you don't drive people like they're driving cars they did. You see once on a time, you was forced to do these things. Well now you're not forced to do nothing. Any good man, you all the time get out of here and make them a dollar. It's your right kind of man. You understand? And you know how to agree with people. You understand me? Which, you do like a man, sure. That woman couldn't give me a thousand dollars for a hold up. No.
No.
